proof_findings.reason: Differentiating the prepaid-stock/discounted-strike representation uses the exact density cancellation. Delta, gamma, vega and calendar theta signs agree with the funded PDE and differentiated put-call parity. Volatility-point scaling, contract multiplier, signed positions and incremental stock trade are explicit. Stock offsets delta without changing option gamma/vega; same S, sigma and tau make the gamma-vega columns dependent even across strikes.

The full multivariate Hessian precedes the abbreviated desk approximation. A compact interior segment and bounded third partials support the cubic full-Taylor bound; omitted mixed/time/volatility quadratic terms remain second order. Differentiating gamma gives C_SSS=-Gamma(1+d1/a)/S; monotone d1 across the spot interval gives the stated conservative maximum. The spot-only theorem is never applied to the mixed example.

The chain rule supplies delta plus vega times stipulated spot response and all four total-gamma terms. A cross-sectional strike skew does not identify that spot response. The text does not treat a calibrated surface partial as a tradable self-financing process or derive untaught stochastic surface dynamics.

Positive vega, continuity and the lower/upper sigma limits prove existence and uniqueness only at strictly interior prices with positive S, K and tau. Lower endpoint is the sigma-zero limit; the upper endpoint has no finite sigma. Zero maturity/stock/strike require nonidentification qualifications. A whole-interval lower-vega bound controls finite perturbations; pointwise inverse vega is local. Floating comparisons, price-resolution statuses and a declared cap are not mislabeled as rigorous interval arithmetic or a universal mathematical restriction.

Vertical bounds use the matched cash discount and payoff inequalities. Unequal-strike weights give a nonnegative triangular butterfly, making the negative quoted cost an arbitrage only for the stipulated executable frictionless contracts. A finite screen pass is not a constructed arbitrage-free joint process, and separate finite IVs do not repair cross-strike inconsistency.

Shares grow through frictionless proportional-dividend reinvestment between declared delta reset dates; cash grows at the financing rate. Each reset deducts the stock trade and, in the fee account, its charged cost. Original wealth is retained rather than overwritten by the new option mark. Terminal error is wealth minus the short-call obligation; earlier fees accumulate to maturity. No extra fee is invented on initial or terminal transactions outside the stated contract.

proof_findings.topic: Continuous volatility mismatch and terminal extension
proof_findings.reason: The actual positive continuous diffusion and continuous adapted coefficients fit c07 before terminal time; pricing sigma and r,q are fixed. Subtracting the funded hedge and option dynamics yields dE=rE dt+Gamma S^2(sigma_bar^2-a_t^2)dt/2. On a finite compact path, S and actual volatility are bounded. Gamma S^2 has a (T-t)^(-1/2) pathwise majorant, with a finite factor for negative q. Bounded delta and localization extend the funded drift/stochastic gains to T; continuous payoff convergence identifies terminal wealth. Expectations still require a separately integrable majorant. The piecewise variance table supplies weights algebraically and is not represented as an actual diffusion or exact discrete realized-variance rule.

Taylor remainder gives M3 h^2/6+epsilon/h for central delta and M4 h^2/12+4epsilon/h^2 for gamma under the declared smooth neighborhood and uniform value error. The optimal h example differentiates its bound correctly. The bounded float API deliberately excludes singular Greek inputs, permits negative rates, rejects negative dividend yield in its narrower lab domain, and honestly reports tiny tail vega underflow. No convergence or market adequacy theorem is inferred from numerical agreement.

worked_case_audit.evidence: Independent terminal-payoff integrals and five-point derivatives reproduce both option values, six Greeks and all signed 1500-unit exposures; per-volatility-point conversion is checked separately.

Independent spot and mixed revaluation confirms 1.5083987665 and 2.1055516424 changes. Spot remainder is inside the analytic bound; the mixed residual exceeds that separate bound. Stipulated response gives total delta about 0.4178318411, and the second total response is independently checked.

Payoff integration at both numerical bracket ends and the midpoint checks sigma about 0.3073774717 for 11.05, its residual and local inverse-vega response. Generated known-volatility quotes and price perturbations provide distinct tests.

Each quoted strike has a finite independently repriced IV, but exact rational slopes are -0.3 and -0.6 and the normalized butterfly costs -1.5. Lowering the middle quote to 9 passes this finite convexity screen only.

Discounted cash balances and dividend-adjusted share units reproduce every ledger field. Terminal ideal and fee-funded errors are about 2.2376042813 and 2.1381380351; the hidden first-reset withdrawal is 1.6340190117. Cost timing remains correct under negative rates and an uneven schedule.

prompt_audit.independent_reasoning: Re-derived density cancellation, both delta formulas, shared gamma/vega and calendar theta parity. Independent payoff integrals/differences reproduce the printed S=85, K=90 case, including vega 23.328217770 per unit sigma and 0.233282178 per point.

Gamma neutrality requires 300 quoted option units, then -80 stock units. Residual vega is -3000 per unit sigma, or -30 for a one-point increase. The fixed S,sigma,tau gamma-vega proportionality proves why strike variation alone cannot furnish independent hedge columns.

Differentiated the exact gamma formula and recovered the conservative C_SSS bound. Recomputed spot change and cubic remainder; mixed Hessian terms named in the solution match all omitted second-order terms of the prompt, so no spot-only certificate is extended to the mixed shock.

Chain rule gives 0.44, then Gamma+2 C_Ssigma sigma_S+C_sigmasigma sigma_S^2+nu sigma_SS. Strike skew is a derivative in a different direction and cannot identify the requested response without a dynamics/sticky-rule assumption.

A symmetric Gaussian density integral gives 80[2Phi(0.1)-1]=6.3724539643 and sigma=0.4. Classified zero, upper-bound, outside-bound and expiry cases separately. Mean value theorem on the stated interval gives 0.05/2=0.025; no pointwise vega is substituted for the interval lower bound.

Recomputed the funded first reset, 1.6340190117 hidden withdrawal under mark overwriting, negative final-95 error -0.6964683234 and financed-cost error -0.7959345696. Later terminal spot changes leave earlier cash decisions unchanged, and all fees accrue from their own dates.

Derived the discounted continuous mismatch identity with drift cancellation and retained financing. Reviewed the pathwise terminal bound and the extra expectation premise. Exact rational variance worksheets give 25/16 and -35/16 despite the same 0.065 time-average variance; their supplied gamma weights are not claimed to be generated hedge trajectories.

Unequal strikes imply weights 3/5 and 2/5 and price -4/5. The piecewise payoff is zero outside [90,115], rises at slope 3/5 to 6, then falls at slope -2/5. Positive per-option IVs cannot eliminate the finite static inconsistency; matched rights and executable prices remain necessary.

Taylor estimates and independent bounded pricing errors produce the stated delta and gamma inequalities. Minimizing the delta bound gives h=0.1 and 0.000015. A common smooth neighborhood and justified uniform pricing-error bound are explicit premises.

All five memo claims receive substantive corrections with at least two numerical counterexamples, a funded/dated hedge plan, bid-ask/rights/dividend assumptions, calibration/evaluation separation and an explicit open-response rubric. The solution addresses each demand without promising empirical dominance or risk-free Greek neutrality.

Answered explanation distinguishes partial Greeks, surface dynamics and funding. Retention answers -48, vega 30 or 0.3 per point, unchanged gamma after stock hedging, no finite upper-bound IV, and a one-unit hidden withdrawal when wealth 7 is forcibly reset to mark 6 are all correct.
